reviewed_exact_row: 30000773 / OWR-1543-004: reciprocally summable edge reinforcement on bounded-degree graphs, including the triangle, eventually traverses one random edge. Original Tarrès/Limic OWR 27/2007 p.1553: https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46113?nt=1

Edge- and vertex-reinforced random walks with super-linear reinforcement on infinite graphs — Codina Cotar and Debleena Thacker; Annals of Probability 45(4) (2017),2655–2706. Prior affirmative attracting-edge result: arbitrary positive finite, possibly nonmonotone reciprocally summable weights; connected undirected bounded-degree graphs and ordinary common finite nonnegative integer initial counts. Theorem 1.1 and finite-graph Theorem 2.4 cover the original question. Inspected arXiv:1509.00807v3; its formula (36) estimate issue and finite-offset correction are retained by PR #1065. Journal body uninspected, no journal-defect allegation. No vertex-reinforcement, arbitrary-real-offset or unbounded-degree extension certified. Existing publication; audit: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1065
